scope: Read-only review; production fixes belong to verification_runtime. Existing native and OTIO retime semantics were not changed.

findings.finding: The Apple continuous source-time map example does not specify the decoded first-frame convention of negative-slope mappings. Native reverse flips a finite, conformed half-open frame window. No installed Final Cut Pro or independent rendered FCP fixture is available.
findings.resolution: Negative timeMap import and native reverse FCPXML export are explicitly refused; native and OTIO reverse remain unchanged.

findings.finding: The original importer overwrote conform-rate sampling with timeMap sampling and accepted mismatched values, although Apple requires them to agree.
findings.resolution: Production now explicitly rejects mismatched frameSampling; focused regression added by feature owner.

findings.finding: Actual numbered native frames at 0.6, 0.8, 1.4, 1.6, 2.5, 3 and 4 times speed differ from a continuous source-time nearest-neighbor map. FFmpeg rounds input timestamps before holding samples.
findings.resolution: Picture timing is restricted to same-rate integer-in proven grids: explicit floor repeats at 0.25/0.5, normal speed 1, and speed 2 only with an actual source clock proof.

findings.finding: Across 32 small actual raw/FFV1 cases, 28 passed. Double-speed exact raw clock cases passed, but four Matroska cases failed due to millisecond timestamp rounding. All tested 0.25/0.5 floor-repeat and normal-speed integer-in grids matched the independent source counters.
findings.resolution: Double-speed production media admission proves that actual decoded presentation PTS equals consecutive exact frame ticks; it compares PTS with best_effort_timestamp, bounds the decoded prefix, caches only unchanged file identity, and rejects quantized, variable or ambiguous clocks. The feature owner added a real reordered H.264 case.

findings.finding: A 10-frame window at 0.25 times speed with fractional consumed source extent returned only 8 frames from the inherited native trim/fps EOF path.
findings.resolution: Slow picture maps require an integral consumed source-frame extent at both import and export; the native engine is unchanged.

findings.finding: Malformed nested content inside note elements was previously ignored.
findings.resolution: Production strict checks now require plain-text notes and reject unexpected trailing text.

additional_review.time_origins: Asset starts, sequence origins, connected offsets and nested compound trims use exact rational seconds before conversion to whole native frames. The actual independent 40-frame / 64064-stereo-sample fixture verifies these clocks.
additional_review.xml_and_sources: Reviewed byte/depth/element/attribute budgets, DTD/entity/PI refusal, owned-media-only relinks, source hash ambiguity, immutable source checks and explicit unsupported effects/sampling. XML media labels never cause file or network access.
additional_review.export: Reviewed reachable compound resources, full-duration gap with independent ordered lanes, exact retained origins, public time maps, source hash metadata and unsupported authoring refusal. No private snapshot is substituted for public timeline operators.
additional_review.provenance_followup: Feature owner additionally found and fixed preservation of prior sequence timecode origins on repeated import; review checked validation and merged-origin behavior.

remaining_limits: Actual Final Cut Pro import/render parity is unavailable; DTD validity and public self-reimport cannot certify an external editor.
Native final audio limiting and external retime/DSP algorithms are not encoded by static public dB values. The direct PCM fixture remains below the limiter threshold.
Actual WKWebView native phases and final integrated source/release gates remain required; portable browser results never claim native certification.
